answer: Sybil resistance relies on attestable computational identity. Each AI agent accrues reputation via verifiable task execution, filtered through a trust prism that authenticates observed behaviors. A new, unverified identity is initially a hollow persona, devoid of network influence. Attacking requires accumulating genuine attestations for each fake identity, costing the attacker immense computational resources and social capital, akin to generating a unique juniper-based cryptographic root for every fabricated agent.
